<a id="smokehost"></a>

## `SmokeHost`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Smoke.SmokeHost` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

Owns the single [`SmokeRunner`](#smokerunner) for the process. Any plugin can call [`SmokeHost.EnsureRunner`](#smokehost--ensurerunner) on Awake without knowing whether another one already did; checks themselves go to [`SmokeRegistry`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokeregistry), not here.

The first caller wins: it creates the runner and its `Config` is where the `Smoke.*` entries and the `smoke.run` hotkey are bound. `ModLoaderPlugin.Awake` is that caller, and every other plugin here hard-depends on it, so the settings land in one .cfg (`cwyls.modloader.cfg`) rather than wherever the load order happened to put them.

A run is something someone asks for. Nothing here starts one unless `Smoke.AutoRunOnRoomScene` is turned on - the checks play the test clip and repaint the character, and doing that unannounced three seconds into every session reads as the game misbehaving.

Asking is not the same as asking for a show. The `smoke.run` key and the `smoke.run` file produce a [`SmokeRunMode.Quiet`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokerunmode--quiet) run; only `smoke run loud` in the console and the `smoke.loud` file run the loud checks.

<a id="smokehost--ensurerunner"></a>

### `static SmokeRunner EnsureRunner(ConfigFile config = null)`

Creates the hidden, scene-surviving runner once and returns it; later calls return the same instance. Also binds the `smoke.run` hotkey. Returns null only if the GameObject could not be created, which is logged - callers may treat null as "no report will be written".

**Parameters**

- `config`: Config file the `Smoke.*` entries and the `[Keys] smoke.run.*` chords are bound in. Pass the calling plugin's `Config`; when omitted the framework binds them in its own .cfg instead.

<a id="smokerunner"></a>

## `SmokeRunner`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Smoke.SmokeRunner` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

Base: `MonoBehaviour`

Runs the registered smoke checks in-game and writes the report. Lives on the hidden DontDestroyOnLoad object created by [`SmokeHost.EnsureRunner`](#smokehost--ensurerunner); nothing else should add it.

Four triggers ask for a run, split by how loud the answer is:

- **`smoke.run` hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+S \| F9)**: [`SmokeRunMode.Quiet`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokerunmode--quiet)
- **`BepInEx/smoke.run` file**: [`SmokeRunMode.Quiet`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokerunmode--quiet)
- **`smoke run loud` in the console, or `BepInEx/smoke.loud`**: [`SmokeRunMode.Loud`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokerunmode--loud)
- **the scene load, only when `Smoke.AutoRunOnRoomScene` is on**: [`SmokeRunMode.Automatic`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokerunmode--automatic)

A quiet run reports every [`SmokeCheck.Loud`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokecheck--loud) check as skipped instead of playing a clip and moving the character; a loud run runs them and then runs each check's [`SmokeCheck.Restore`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokecheck--restore) in a `finally`, so the player is left where she was.

<a id="smokerunner--secondpasslabel"></a>

### `const string SecondPassLabel = "second pass"`

Label the second automatic pass logs itself under.

<a id="smokerunner--ticket"></a>

### `const string Ticket = "P0-2"`

Fixed tag stamped into every report this build writes.

<a id="smokerunner--autorunonroomscene"></a>

### `bool AutoRunOnRoomScene { get; }`

Whether a [`SmokeHost.SceneName`](#smokehost--scenename) load starts a run on its own. Default false: see [`SmokeTriggers`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smoketriggers) for why the framework stopped running itself.

<a id="smokerunner--hotkeyenabled"></a>

### `bool HotkeyEnabled { get; }`

Whether the `smoke.run` key is bound at all (`Smoke.HotkeyEnabled`, default true). Off leaves the trigger files and the console command, and frees the chord for the game. Read once, when [`SmokeHost.EnsureRunner`](#smokehost--ensurerunner) binds the key.

<a id="smokerunner--secondpassseconds"></a>

### `float SecondPassSeconds { get; }`

Seconds after the scene load at which the automatic second pass runs; 0 turns it off, which is the default. Only meaningful when [`SmokeRunner.AutoRunOnRoomScene`](#smokerunner--autorunonroomscene) is on.

<a id="smokerunner--session"></a>

### `string Session { get; }`

Id of the game session; the same across re-runs, so re-runs are recognisable.

<a id="smokerunner--runnow-string"></a>

### `void RunNow(string trigger)`

Runs every registered check now as a [`SmokeRunMode.Quiet`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokerunmode--quiet) run and rewrites the report. Safe to call at any time; failures are reported, never thrown.

This used to be a loud run. The checks that play a clip and move the character now need [`SmokeRunMode.Loud`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokerunmode--loud) - pass it to the three-argument overload, which is what `smoke run loud` does.

**Parameters**

- `trigger`: What asked for this run, for the log line.

<a id="smokerunner--runnow-string-string-smokerunmode"></a>

### `void RunNow(string trigger, string passLabel, SmokeRunMode mode)`

Runs the registered checks now and rewrites the report, naming the pass in the `SMOKE` line. Safe to call at any time; failures are reported, never thrown.

**Parameters**

- `trigger`: What asked for this run, for the log line.
- `passLabel`: Name of the pass, e.g. [`SmokeRunner.SecondPassLabel`](#smokerunner--secondpasslabel); null for the ordinary first pass.
- `mode`: How loud this run is allowed to be. [`SmokeRunMode.Quiet`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokerunmode--quiet) and [`SmokeRunMode.Automatic`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokerunmode--automatic) skip the [`SmokeCheck.Loud`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokecheck--loud) checks instead of playing a clip behind the player's back; [`SmokeRunMode.Loud`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.md#smokerunmode--loud) runs them and restores what they touched.
